question: Today is Monday. What day of the week will it be the day after tomorrow?
solution: Tomorrow is Tuesday, and the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.

A.text: Sunday was yesterday. The question asks about a later day.

C.text: Monday is today.

D.text: Tuesday is tomorrow. The day after tomorrow is one day later.

E.text: Thursday is three days after Monday, not two.

question: Tom is 6 years old. How old will he be in 3 years?
solution: Each year Tom gets one year older: 7, 8, 9. In 3 years he will be 9.

A.text: 3 is the number of years that pass.

B.text: 6 is Tom's age now.

D.text: Count on 3 years from 6: 7, 8, 9.

E.text: You multiplied 6 by 3. Add 3 years instead.

question: Yesterday was Friday. What day of the week is it today?
solution: The day after Friday is Saturday, so today is Saturday.

A.text: Thursday comes before Friday. Today comes after yesterday.

B.text: Friday was yesterday.

C.text: Sunday is tomorrow.

E.text: Monday is the day after tomorrow.

question: A week has 7 days. How many days are there in 2 weeks?
solution: Two weeks are 7 + 7 = 14 days.

A.text: 2 is the number of weeks.

B.text: 7 days is only one week.

C.text: You added 7 and 2. Add 7 days for each week.

D.text: 21 days is 3 weeks.

question: Anna is 8 years old and her brother is 5. How many years older than her brother is Anna?
solution: 8 - 5 = 3. Anna is 3 years older.

B.text: 5 is her brother's age.

C.text: 8 is Anna's age.

D.text: You added the ages. Take the smaller from the bigger.

E.text: You multiplied the ages.

question: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week was it 3 days ago?
solution: Going back from Wednesday: Tuesday, Monday, Sunday. 3 days ago it was Sunday.

A.text: Saturday is 3 days after Wednesday. The question asks about 3 days ago.

B.text: Monday was 2 days ago.

D.text: Tuesday was yesterday, only 1 day ago.

E.text: Thursday is tomorrow.

question: In 4 years Mia will be 11 years old. How old is she now?
solution: Now she is 4 years younger than she will be: 11 - 4 = 7.

A.text: 4 is the number of years.

B.text: 11 is her age in 4 years, not now.

C.text: Now she is younger than in 4 years, so take 4 away.

E.text: You multiplied 11 by 4.

question: The holidays last from Monday to the next Sunday, including both of these days. How many days do the holidays last?
solution: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: that is 7 days.

A.text: 2 is the number of days named in the question.

B.text: Both Monday and Sunday are holidays, so count them both: 7 days.

C.text: From Monday to the next Sunday there are 7 days, not 8.

D.text: You doubled 7. The holidays last one week.

question: Kate's birthday is on 5 May. Today is 28 April. April has 30 days. How many days are left until her birthday?
solution: From 28 April to 30 April is 2 days, and from 30 April to 5 May is 5 more days. 2 + 5 = 7 days.

B.text: 5 is the date of the birthday.

C.text: Count the days: 29 and 30 April, then 1 to 5 May. That is 7.

D.text: April has 30 days, not 31.

E.text: You took 5 from 28. The dates are in different months.

question: Grandpa is 60 years old. Dad is 35. How old was Grandpa when Dad was born?
solution: Grandpa is 60 - 35 = 25 years older than Dad. When Dad was born, Grandpa was 25.

A.text: You took 30 from 60. The difference between the ages is 60 - 35.

C.text: 35 is Dad's age now.

D.text: 60 is Grandpa's age now.

E.text: You added the ages.

question: Today is Tuesday. What day of the week will it be in 10 days?
solution: In 7 days it will be Tuesday again. 3 more days give Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. So it will be Friday.

A.text: Wednesday is only 1 day after Tuesday.

B.text: You counted today as the first day. In 10 days it will be Friday.

C.text: In 7 days it is Tuesday again, then 3 more days: Friday.

E.text: 10 days is one week and 3 days, not one week and 5 days.

question: Ann is 3 years older than Ben. In 5 years Ben will be 12. How old is Ann now?
solution: Ben is 12 - 5 = 7 now. Ann is 3 years older: 7 + 3 = 10.

A.text: 7 is Ben's age now. Ann is 3 years older.

B.text: 12 is Ben's age in 5 years.

C.text: 15 is Ann's age in 5 years, not now.

D.text: You added 12, 5 and 3. Ben is younger now, so take 5 away.

question: A month has 30 days, and its 1st day is a Monday. What day of the week is the 15th?
solution: The 8th is a Monday, one week after the 1st. The 15th is one more week later: also a Monday.

B.text: The 15th is exactly 2 weeks after the 1st, so it is a Monday.

C.text: You added 15 days to the 1st. The 15th is only 14 days after the 1st.

D.text: Count by weeks: the 1st, 8th and 15th are all Mondays.

E.text: The 1st is a Monday, so every 7 days later is a Monday too.

question: Olya goes swimming every 3 days: on the 2nd, the 5th, the 8th and so on. How many times does she go swimming in a month of 30 days?
solution: The days are 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26 and 29. That is 10 times.

A.text: List the days: 2, 5, ..., 29. There are 10 of them.

C.text: The next day would be the 32nd, which is not in the month.

D.text: You halved 30. She goes every 3 days, not every 2.

E.text: 30 is the number of days in the month.

question: Sasha was born in 2019. In which year will Sasha turn 10?
solution: Sasha turns 10 ten years after being born: 2019 + 10 = 2029.

A.text: 2009 is 10 years before Sasha was born.

B.text: 2019 is the year Sasha was born.

D.text: In 2020 Sasha turns 1.

E.text: In 2030 Sasha turns 11.

question: Today is Sunday. What day of the week will it be in 20 days?
solution: In 14 days, two weeks, it is Sunday again. 6 more days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.

A.text: 20 days is 2 weeks and 6 days, not 2 weeks and 5 days.

B.text: 21 days would give Sunday again; 20 days is one day earlier.

C.text: Monday is 22 days after Sunday.

D.text: 20 days is 2 weeks and 6 days. Count the 6 extra days from Sunday.

question: The ages of two sisters add up to 15. What will their ages add up to in 3 years?
solution: In 3 years each sister will be 3 years older, so the sum grows by 3 + 3 = 6: 15 + 6 = 21.

B.text: 15 is the sum now.

C.text: Each of the two sisters gets 3 years older, not only one.

D.text: The sum grows by 3 for each sister: 6, not 9.

E.text: You multiplied 15 by 3.

question: A month has 31 days, and its 1st day is a Saturday. How many Sundays are there in this month?
solution: The Sundays are the 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th. That is 5 Sundays.

C.text: You forgot the 30th.

D.text: The next Sunday after the 30th would be the 37th.

E.text: 31 is the number of days.

question: Ben is 5 years old and his mum is 29. In how many years will Mum be exactly 3 times as old as Ben?
solution: Try year by year. In 7 years Ben will be 12 and Mum will be 36, and 36 = 3 × 12.

A.text: 3 is how many times older Mum will be.

B.text: 5 is Ben's age now.

D.text: In 9 years Ben is 14 and Mum is 38, which is not 3 × 14.

E.text: 24 is how many years older Mum is than Ben.

question: A school trip starts on a Thursday and lasts 5 days, counting the first day. On which day of the week does it end?
solution: The days are Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday and Monday. It ends on Monday.

A.text: Saturday is only the 3rd day of the trip.

B.text: Sunday is the 4th day. Count 5 days: Thursday to Monday.

C.text: The first day, Thursday, is already one of the 5 days.

E.text: Wednesday would be the 7th day of the trip.

question: Today is Friday. What day of the week was it 100 days ago?
solution: 98 days are exactly 14 weeks, so 98 days ago it was also Friday. 2 more days back: Thursday, Wednesday.

B.text: 100 days is 14 weeks and 2 days, not 3 days.

C.text: 100 days is 14 weeks and 2 days, not 1 day.

D.text: Ago means going back, not forward.

E.text: Sunday is 100 days after Friday, not before.

question: Kolya is 8 and his sister is 3. How old will Kolya be when he is exactly twice as old as his sister?
solution: Kolya is always 5 years older than his sister. He is twice as old as her when she is 5 and he is 10.

A.text: 5 is how many years older Kolya is.

C.text: 6 is twice his sister's age now, not Kolya's age.

D.text: At 12 his sister would be 7, and 12 is not twice 7.

E.text: You doubled Kolya's age now. His sister grows older too.

question: In some year, 1 January was a Monday. January has 31 days. What day of the week was 1 February?
solution: 28 days after 1 January, on 29 January, it is Monday again. 1 February is 3 days later: Thursday.

A.text: 31 days is not a whole number of weeks: 4 weeks and 3 days.

B.text: 31 days is 4 weeks and 3 days: you added only 1 day.

D.text: 31 days is 4 weeks and 3 days, not 2 days.

E.text: 31 days is 4 weeks and 3 days, not 4 days.

question: Twins Ann and Kate and their brother Tom are 23 years old altogether. Tom is 5 years older than each twin. How old is Tom?
solution: If Tom were 5 years younger, all three would be the same age and together 23 - 5 = 18. So each twin is 6, and Tom is 6 + 5 = 11.

A.text: 6 is the age of each twin. Tom is 5 years older.

B.text: You shared 18 between 2 children, but there are 3.

C.text: If Tom were 12, the twins would be 7 and the total would be 26.

E.text: 18 is the total of three equal ages, not Tom's age.

question: This year Masha's birthday is on a Wednesday. Next year her birthday comes 365 days later. On which day of the week will it be?
solution: 365 days are 52 weeks and 1 day. After 52 weeks it is Wednesday again, and 1 more day gives Thursday.

A.text: The birthday moves forward, not back.

B.text: 365 days are not a whole number of weeks: 52 weeks and 1 day.

C.text: That would be after 366 days, in a leap year.

D.text: 365 days are 52 weeks and 1 day, not 3 days.

question: Today is Thursday. What day of the week will it be in 15 days?
solution: In 14 days, two weeks, it is Thursday again. 1 more day gives Friday.

A.text: The day comes after today, not before.

B.text: 15 days is 2 weeks and 1 day, not a whole number of weeks.

C.text: 15 days is 2 weeks and 1 day, not 2 weeks and 2 days.

E.text: You added 5 days for the 15. Count weeks: 2 weeks and 1 day.

question: Dad is 36 years old and his son is 9. How many times as old as his son is Dad?
solution: 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Dad is 4 times as old as his son.

C.text: 27 is how many years older Dad is.

D.text: You added the ages.

question: How many days are there in March, April and May together?
solution: March has 31 days, April 30 and May 31. 31 + 30 + 31 = 92.

B.text: 3 is the number of months.

C.text: March and May have 31 days, not 30.

D.text: Only April has 30 days; March and May have 31 each.

E.text: April has 30 days, not 31.

question: A leap year has 366 days. How many full weeks are there in a leap year?
solution: 52 weeks are 364 days. 366 - 364 = 2 days are left, which is not a full week. So there are 52 full weeks.

A.text: 12 is the number of months.

C.text: 51 weeks are only 357 days; one more full week fits.

D.text: 53 weeks would be 371 days, more than 366.

E.text: 366 is the number of days.

question: Grandma was born in 1958. How old will she be on her birthday in 2026?
solution: 2026 - 1958 = 68. On her birthday in 2026 she turns 68.

A.text: 58 is the end of her birth year, not her age.

E.text: Check the subtraction: 1958 + 68 = 2026.

question: 1 September is a Monday. September has 30 days. What day of the week is 1 October?
solution: 28 days after 1 September, on 29 September, it is Monday again. 1 October is 2 days later: Wednesday.

A.text: 30 days are 4 weeks and 2 days, not whole weeks.

B.text: 30 days are 4 weeks and 2 days, not 1 day.

C.text: September has 30 days, not 31.

D.text: 30 days are 4 weeks and 2 days. Count 2 days on from Monday.

question: Three years ago Vera was 7. How old will she be in 4 years?
solution: Now Vera is 7 + 3 = 10. In 4 years she will be 10 + 4 = 14.

B.text: 4 is the number of years ahead.

C.text: 7 was her age three years ago.

D.text: 10 is her age now.

E.text: You added only 4 to 7. First find her age now.

question: A festival lasts from 25 June to 5 July, including both days. June has 30 days. How many days does the festival last?
solution: From 25 to 30 June there are 6 days, and from 1 to 5 July there are 5 days. 6 + 5 = 11.

A.text: Both 25 June and 5 July count: 6 + 5 = 11.

C.text: June has 30 days, not 31.

D.text: You took 5 from 25. The dates are in different months.

E.text: 30 is the number of days in June.

question: Mum is 4 times as old as Petya. Together they are 40 years old. How old is Petya?
solution: Mum's age is 4 parts and Petya's is 1 part: 5 parts make 40, so 1 part is 8. Petya is 8.

A.text: 4 is how many times as old Mum is.

B.text: You divided 40 by 4, but together they make 5 parts.

D.text: 32 is Mum's age.

E.text: You took 4 from 40.

question: The 1st of a month is a Sunday. On which date is the third Wednesday of the month?
solution: The first Wednesday is the 4th. The second is the 11th, and the third is the 18th.

A.text: The 11th is the second Wednesday.

B.text: The 17th is a Tuesday.

C.text: You multiplied 3 by 7. The first Wednesday is the 4th, not the 7th.

E.text: The 25th is the fourth Wednesday.

question: In some year 1 March is a Tuesday. What day of the week is 1 June of the same year?
solution: March has 31 days, April 30 and May 31: 92 days in all. 91 days are 13 weeks, so 1 June is 1 day after Tuesday: Wednesday.

B.text: Count forward from March to June, not back.

C.text: 92 days are 13 weeks and 1 day, not whole weeks.

D.text: April has 30 days, not 31.

E.text: 92 days are 13 weeks and 1 day. Add just 1 day.

question: Olya is now 3 times as old as her brother. In 4 years she will be twice as old as him. How old is Olya now?
solution: Try the brother's age. If he is 4, Olya is 12. In 4 years he is 8 and she is 16, which is twice 8. So Olya is 12.

A.text: 4 is her brother's age.

C.text: 8 is her brother's age in 4 years.

D.text: 16 is Olya's age in 4 years, not now.

E.text: If Olya were 24, her brother would be 8; in 4 years 28 is not twice 12.

question: What is the greatest number of Saturdays that one month can have?
solution: A month has at most 31 days: 4 weeks and 3 days. So a day of the week can appear at most 5 times.

A.text: A month has more than 28 days, so some days of the week appear 5 times.

B.text: 6 Saturdays need at least 36 days.

D.text: 7 is the number of days in a week.

E.text: 31 is the number of days in the longest months.

question: Anya was born on 29 February 2016. This date exists only in leap years: 2020, 2024 and every fourth year after that. How many birthdays on the real date will she have from 2017 to 2032, including 2032?
solution: The leap years are 2020, 2024, 2028 and 2032. That is 4 birthdays.

A.text: 2032 counts too.

B.text: 2016 is the year she was born, not a birthday.

C.text: Leap years come every 4 years, not every 2.

E.text: 16 is the number of years from 2016 to 2032.

question: The day before yesterday was Thursday. What day of the week will it be the day after tomorrow?
solution: Yesterday was Friday, so today is Saturday. Tomorrow is Sunday, and the day after tomorrow is Monday.

A.text: Friday was yesterday.

B.text: Saturday is today.

C.text: Sunday is tomorrow.

D.text: Tuesday is 3 days after today.

question: In a year that is not a leap year, 1 January is a Friday. What day of the week is 31 December?
solution: 31 December is 364 days after 1 January. 364 days are exactly 52 weeks, so it is also a Friday.

A.text: 364 days are exactly 52 weeks, so the day of the week does not change.

C.text: Saturday would be 365 days later, but 31 December is 364 days after 1 January.

D.text: 364 days are exactly 52 weeks.

E.text: From 1 January to 31 December there are 364 days: 52 whole weeks.

question: Three brothers are 5, 8 and 11 years old. In how many years will their ages add up to 60?
solution: Now their ages add up to 24. Every year the sum grows by 3. It must grow by 60 - 24 = 36, which takes 36 ÷ 3 = 12 years.

A.text: In 13 years the sum would be 24 + 39 = 63.

B.text: You divided 60 by 3. Start from the sum now, 24.

D.text: 36 is how much the sum must grow. Each year it grows by 3.

E.text: 60 is the sum they must reach.

question: A month has 5 Fridays and 5 Saturdays, but only 4 Thursdays and 4 Sundays. What day of the week is the 1st of this month?
solution: A month is 4 full weeks plus 0 to 3 extra days, and only the days of the week of the extra days appear 5 times. Here only Friday and Saturday appear 5 times, so the month has 30 days and starts on a Friday.

A.text: If the 1st were a Thursday, there would be 5 Thursdays.

B.text: If the 1st were a Saturday, there would be 5 Sundays instead of 5 Fridays.

C.text: If the 1st were a Sunday, there would be 5 Sundays.

E.text: If the 1st were a Monday, Friday and Saturday could not both appear 5 times.

question: Masha's grandma is 7 times as old as Masha. In 5 years she will be 5 times as old as Masha. How old is Masha now?
solution: Try Masha's age. If she is 10, Grandma is 70. In 5 years Masha is 15 and Grandma is 75, and 75 = 5 × 15. So Masha is 10.

A.text: 5 is the number of years.

B.text: 15 is Masha's age in 5 years.

C.text: 60 is how many years older Grandma is.

D.text: 70 is Grandma's age now.

question: School holidays start on Saturday, 26 October, and last 9 days, counting the first day. October has 31 days. On which day do the holidays end?
solution: The holidays are 26, 27, 28, 29, 30 and 31 October, then 1, 2 and 3 November: 9 days. 26 October is a Saturday, so 2 November is a Saturday too and 3 November is a Sunday.

B.text: That is only the 8th day of the holidays.

C.text: October has 31 days, so the 9th day is 3 November.

D.text: That would be the 10th day of the holidays.

E.text: That is when the holidays start.

question: 1 January 2026 is a Thursday. The years 2026 and 2027 have 365 days each, and 2028 is a leap year with 366 days. What day of the week is 1 January 2029?
solution: 365 days are 52 weeks and 1 day, and 366 days are 52 weeks and 2 days. From 1 January 2026 to 1 January 2029 the day moves on 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 days: Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday.

A.text: 2028 is a leap year, so it moves the day by 2, not 1.

B.text: The day moves by 1 + 1 + 2 = 4, not 5.

D.text: Only 2028 is a leap year; 2026 and 2027 move the day by 1 each.

E.text: 365 days are 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day of the week changes every year.

question: A boy is as many months old as his grandfather is years old. Together they are 65 years old. How old is the boy in years?
solution: A year has 12 months, so the grandfather is 12 times as old as the boy. Their ages are 1 part and 12 parts, 13 parts in all. 65 ÷ 13 = 5. The boy is 5 and the grandfather is 60.

A.text: If the boy were 6, the grandfather would be 72 and together they would be 78.

B.text: 12 is how many months are in a year, not the boy's age.

C.text: 13 is the number of equal parts, not the age.

E.text: 60 is the grandfather's age.

question: In some year, 10 March is a Tuesday. March has 31 days and April has 30. What day of the week is 10 May of the same year?
solution: From 10 March to 10 April is 31 days, and from 10 April to 10 May is 30 days: 61 days. 56 days are 8 weeks, so 10 May is 5 days after Tuesday: Sunday.

A.text: 61 days are 8 weeks and 5 days, not 4 days.

B.text: April has 30 days, not 31.

C.text: 61 days are not a whole number of weeks.

D.text: You moved 2 days for the 2 months. Count all 61 days.

question: Four children were born exactly one year apart. Their ages now add up to 42. How old is the oldest child?
solution: If all four were as old as the youngest, the sum would be 42 - (1 + 2 + 3) = 36, so the youngest is 9. The others are 10, 11 and 12. The oldest is 12.

B.text: 9 is the youngest child.

C.text: You shared 42 equally among 4 children, but their ages are different.

D.text: 11 is the second oldest child.

E.text: If the oldest were 13, the ages 10, 11, 12 and 13 would add up to 46.

question: In a leap year of 366 days, 1 January is a Saturday. How many Saturdays are there in this year?
solution: 366 days are 52 weeks and 2 days. The 52 weeks hold 52 Saturdays, and the 2 extra days at the end are a Saturday and a Sunday. 52 + 1 = 53.

A.text: 52 full weeks already give 52 Saturdays.

C.text: 2 days are left after 52 weeks, and one of them is a Saturday.

D.text: Only one of the two extra days is a Saturday.

E.text: 366 is the number of days.
